speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are suffering from chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to help me identify the cause, how long have these symptoms been present and have there been any blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Campylobacter jejuni enteritis (or other infectious colitis).

Based on your camping history and the presence of mucus, urgency, and a feeling of incomplete evacuation, this presentation is highly suggestive of infectious colitis. Could you clarify if you have a fever or night sweats, and have you had any recent antibiotic use? Additionally, I will need to see a stool culture result to confirm the specific pathogen. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Culture_and_Sensitivity.
